title: How Retail Loses Money in Option Trading | QuantPedia
summary: Summary of a study finding retail options traders pile into high-volatility earnings announcements, overpay, hold losers too long, and transfer wealth to market makers.

assertions.quote: incur large losses from bidding up prices for options of firms whose announcements are expected to trigger greater abnormal volatility
Retail losses from bidding up prices are compounded by enormous bid-ask spreads in options ahead of high expected volatility announcements.
retail traders appear reluctant to close their option positions following high EAV earnings announcements

verdicts.note: The study documents a disposition-effect pattern consistent with the broader retail-investor behaviour literature.

assertions.quote: retail investors are attracted to high EAV announcements because of a preference for positively-skewed, i.e., lottery-like payoffs
increasing more than ten-fold over the past decade in terms of dollar volume traded

verdicts.note: Exchange and wholesaler data show retail option volume surged after 2019 with zero-commission brokers.

assertions.quote: Market makers are the primary beneficiaries of these patterns
retail tends to gravitate towards firms with more media coverage

verdicts.note: Barber and Odean's attention-driven trading finding is well replicated.

Retail share in options is higher on smaller, higher-volume underlyings and correlates with WallStreetBets mentions and Robinhood ownership, consistent with attention-grabbing names; media coverage per se is not measured.
